# @abpilot/cli

A small local web UI for ABPilot. It keeps only three capabilities from the
reference Axiom UI host:

- **Gateway integration** — discovers the running ABPilot desktop daemon from
  `~/.abpilot/desktop/runtime.json`, reports daemon/routes/services, and proxies
  HTTP/WebSocket traffic under `/gateway/*`.
- **OpenCode AI chat** — starts a private `opencode serve` process per UI
  session, reverse-proxies it under `/opencode`, and exposes the chat bridge to
  skill apps.
- **Skill apps** — discovers `app/` directories in skill roots, serves static
  apps under `/<name>/iframe`, and lets JS skill apps mount APIs, WebSockets, and
  UI entries under `/<name>`.

It intentionally does **not** include Axiom login, notifications, SurrealDB,
iroh peer management, or the Axiom link/router configuration. The gateway is the
only transport integration. Skill apps may declare their own login; the UI only
mirrors the reported account in the sidebar and never stores credentials.

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 20
- An ABPilot desktop daemon for gateway integration (optional; the UI still
  starts without it, and AI chat can run independently)
- `opencode` is provided by the `@opencode/cli` dependency, or can be overridden
  with `--opencode-bin`

## Install / run

```bash
cd cli
npm install
npm run build:ui
node bin/abpilot.js ui
```

From the repository root, `npm run daemon` starts the same UI with the
desktop-provided `PORT`. ABPilot Desktop can therefore use the repo root as a
workspace with its default service command.

During development:

```bash
# terminal 1: UI dev server (proxies /api, /opencode, /gateway to 17622)
cd cli/ui && npm install && npm run dev

# terminal 2: backend
cd cli && node bin/abpilot.js ui --no-open
```

The UI listens on `http://127.0.0.1:17622` by default. Use `--port`, `--host`,
or `ABPILOT_UI_PORT` to change it. When launched as a desktop-managed service
(`ABPILOT_DESKTOP=1`), it uses the allocated `PORT` and does not open a browser;
an explicit `--port` still wins.

### Layout

- Desktop: a fixed sidebar (collapsible to an icon rail) next to the content
  pane, with the theme switch and AI-chat toggle in the top-right corner.
- Up to 819px wide the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer with a backdrop and
  a menu button in the content header; the drawer starts open when no skill app
  is selected. AI chat takes the whole screen instead of shrinking the
  workspace, and touch targets are at least 44px.
- A phone opens AI chat first: the shell treats `ABPILOT.platform` of `ios` or
  `android` (or the compact layout on a touch device) as the mobile entry and
  starts with the chat panel open. An explicit deep link to a skill app keeps
  that app visible instead.
- When the user agent contains `Abpilot/` (the mobile app appends it, and the
  `window.ABPILOT` bridge is present) the host overlays its own three-dot menu
  in the top-right corner of the WebView. The header and chat actions then keep
  that 64px corner clear instead of sitting underneath it.
- In that client the account belongs to the app, not to a skill app's desktop
  session. The shell reads `ABPILOT.getLoginUser()`/`ABPILOT.user`, starts
  `ABPILOT.login()` once when the app is signed out, and follows
  `abpilot:user` as the user signs in or out. The footer shows the app profile;
  the token and auth service URL never cross the bridge.
- The page owns the safe areas of the iOS app's full-bleed WebView: the side
  bar, content header, chat panel and the embedded workspace frame are padded by
  `env(safe-area-inset-*)` (kept in `--safe-*` variables, and enabled by the
  `viewport-fit=cover` meta). They resolve to zero in a desktop browser and
  inside an already-inset Android WebView, so nothing shifts there.
- Phone inputs use a 16px font so iOS does not zoom the page on focus. While a
  text field (or the keyboard) is focused the shell tags the document and the
  chat panel drops its bottom inset, because the keyboard already covers the
  home indicator and would otherwise leave an empty band above it.

## Commands

```text
abpilot ui [options]
abpilot gateway [status|routes|services|url] [options]
abpilot --version
abpilot --help
```

`abpilot ui` options:

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-p, --port <port>` | Listen port (default `17622`, `0` picks a free port) |
| `-H, --host <host>` | Listen address (default `127.0.0.1`) |
| `-g, --gateway <url>` | Gateway URL; overrides `runtime.json` |
| `--runtime <file>` | Desktop `runtime.json` path |
| `--cwd <dir>` | Workspace for OpenCode and skill discovery |
| `--skills-dir <dir>` | Extra skill root; may be repeated |
| `--state-file <file>` | UI state file (default `~/.abpilot/cli/state.json`) |
| `--opencode-bin <path>` | Explicit `opencode` executable |
| `--no-opencode` | Do not start AI chat |
| `--no-open` | Do not open the browser |

Examples:

```bash
abpilot ui
abpilot ui --port 17630 --no-open
abpilot ui --gateway http://127.0.0.1:54067
abpilot gateway status
abpilot gateway status --json
abpilot gateway routes
abpilot gateway url /<endpointId>/<workdir>/api
```

## Gateway discovery

The CLI reads the desktop runtime file:

```text
~/.abpilot/desktop/runtime.json
```

It uses:

- `daemon.gatewayUrl` for the loopback gateway
- `daemon.apiUrl` for `/built-in/v1/daemon/status` and `/routes`
- `builtinUrl` for `/built-in/v1/services`
- `builtinToken` as the `x-abpilot-builtin-token` header on every desktop
  built-in request (the file is mode `0600` and the token is per-process)
- `daemon.endpointId` for display and helper URLs

Override the path with `--runtime` or `ABPILOT_RUNTIME_FILE`, or the whole
desktop data directory with `ABPILOT_DESKTOP_DIR`. If the desktop app is not
running, pass `--gateway` explicitly or start the desktop app first.

### HTTP and WebSocket proxy

Requests to `/gateway/<path>` are streamed to `<gatewayUrl>/<path>` without
decompressing bodies. WebSocket upgrades on `/gateway/<path>` are bridged to the
gateway as well. This lets skill apps use a same-origin URL even though the
gateway only listens on loopback.

### External access through the desktop gateway

`abpilot ui` registers itself with the running ABPilot desktop host as an
**exposure**. An exposure is a loopback UI published at:

```text
<gatewayUrl>/<endpointId>/<workdirHash>/
```

The desktop assigns a synthetic `workdirHash`, pushes the route to the daemon,
and returns the external URL. Registration is automatic when
`builtinUrl` is present in `runtime.json`. It requires a desktop build with the
`/built-in/v1/exposures` API; older builds keep the UI local-only.

External access is **off by default**:

- The UI stores `enabled: false` on first run.
- While disabled, no daemon route is published and the UI also rejects any
  request carrying `x-abpilot-endpoint-id` with `403`.
- External access is managed from the desktop host, not from the CLI UI. The
  exposure path is portable across gateways; the full URL uses the local gateway
  port.

The daemon strips the external `/<endpoint>/<workdir>` prefix before forwarding
to this UI, so the UI always sees normal root-relative paths. The CLI does not
inject a base path or rewrite HTML; the built UI uses relative assets and hash
routing, and skill apps should use relative URLs inside their iframe.

Exposures have a heartbeat (20 s, 2 min TTL). A crashed CLI therefore stops
being routed automatically; a clean shutdown deletes the exposure immediately.

### Skill app context

JS skill apps receive `gateway` in their context:

```js
export default function init(app, ctx) {
  ctx.gateway.url();                 // http://127.0.0.1:54067
  ctx.gateway.endpointId();
  ctx.gateway.status();              // status/routes/services snapshot
  ctx.gateway.routes();
  ctx.gateway.services();
  ctx.gateway.fetch("/<endpoint>/<workdir>/...");
  ctx.gateway.wsUrl("/<endpoint>/<workdir>/...");
  ctx.gateway.proxyPath("/<endpoint>/<workdir>/..."); // /gateway/...
  ctx.gateway.urlFor(endpoint, workdir, "/suffix");
}
```

`ctx.external` lets a skill app inspect or narrow its own external surface:

```js
export default function init(app, ctx) {
  ctx.external.status();          // availability, enabled, endpoint, URL
  ctx.external.enabled();
  ctx.external.url("/api/public"); // external URL for this skill app
  ctx.external.policy();          // current policy
  ctx.external.capabilities();    // { chat, gateway, skills }
  ctx.external.configure({
    enabled: true,
    allow: ["/my-skill", "/my-skill/iframe", "/my-skill/api/public"],
    deny: ["/my-skill/api/private"],
  });
  ctx.external.configureCapabilities({ chat: false, gateway: false });
  ctx.external.allowSkill("other-skill", false); // per-skill grant
  // Accept extra external callers (null revokes). Consulted for every external
  // request, even while the global external toggle is off; local-only host APIs
  // still reject accepted callers.
  ctx.external.authorize(async ({ endpointId }) => endpointId === knownPeer);
  // A login extension answers denied document navigations itself (return true
  // once handled). Only for `Accept: text/html` navigations; everything else
  // keeps the host's denial.
  ctx.external.gate((req, res) => {
    res.status(200).type("html").send(signInPage);
    return true;
  });
}
```

`ctx.store` is the UI's shared local store (`~/.abpilot/cli/state.json` by
default), namespaced per skill app so two apps cannot see each other's keys:

```js
export default async function init(app, ctx) {
  await ctx.store.set("session", { token: "..." });
  await ctx.store.get("session");    // value or null
  await ctx.store.keys();            // keys in this app's namespace
  await ctx.store.all();             // the whole namespace
  await ctx.store.delete("session");
}
```

Values are JSON. Writes are serialized and atomic with the rest of the UI
state, so a skill can persist a session or a cache without adding another file
or database.

The same policy can be declared in `package.json`:

```json
{
  "abpilot": {
    "plugin": "index.js",
    "external": {
      "enabled": true,
      "allow": ["/my-skill", "/my-skill/iframe", "/my-skill/api/public"],
      "deny": []
    }
  }
}
```

Policies are enforced by the host for every external request. A policy may
also carry top-level `allow`/`deny` lists for all paths; `skills.<name>` narrows
one app. `deny` always wins, and a non-empty `allow` list restricts the surface
to those path prefixes. Policy paths are decoded, lowercased, and rejected on
`..` segments before matching, so `/OPENCODE` or `/%6fpenode` cannot slip past a
`/opencode` rule.

`capabilities.skills` is **opt-in**: enabling external access exposes chat and
gateway only, and skill apps (account sessions, credentials, device lists) stay
local until `skills: true` is set explicitly.
External policy changes are local-only (`POST /api/external` is rejected for
iroh requests), so a remote peer cannot widen its own access.

A skill app can also register a **caller authorizer** with
`ctx.external.authorize(fn)`. The host runs it for external requests and, when
it returns `true`, serves the request as the workspace owner: path/skill denies
are bypassed, the skill list is not filtered, and the request is marked
`req.abpilotOwner`. This is how the Account skill lets endpoints registered to
the same signed-in user use the whole workspace. The authorizer works even while
the global external toggle is off — it widens access for the callers it accepts
rather than turning external access on — and it cannot reach local-only host
APIs, which keep rejecting external requests after the guard. Failures and
timeouts deny.

A login extension can also answer the callers nobody accepted. `ctx.external.gate(fn)`
registers a handler for denied document navigations (`Accept: text/html`,
`GET`/`HEAD`); the host calls it instead of sending its 403 page, and the
handler returns `true` once it responded. This is how the Account skill shows
its sign-in screen: the page calls `ABPILOT.login()` in the caller's WebView,
the app registers that device's endpoint, and the authorizer admits it on the
next load. The gate answers on the requested path — a redirect would drop the
daemon's `/<endpoint>/<workdir>` prefix — and every other request keeps the
host's denial (`401 sign_in_required` for non-navigation requests, the 403 page
when no gate is registered or it fails).

## Skill apps

Roots are scanned in this order (local project roots first):

```text
./.abpilot/skills
./skills
./.agents/skills
./.opencode/skills
./.claude/skills
./.cursor/skills
./.codex/skills
~/.abpilot/skills
~/.agents/skills
~/.axiom/skills
~/.claude/skills
... other common AI tool skill roots
```

A skill app is either:

### Static app

```text
skills/<skill-name>/
  app/
    index.html
    assets/...
```

It is served at `/<skill-name>/iframe/` and appears in the sidebar.

### JS skill app

```text
skills/<skill-name>/
  app/
    package.json
    index.js
```

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "my-skill-app",
  "abpilot": {
    "plugin": "index.js",
    "title": "My Skill",
    "icon": "app",
    "description": "Does something useful"
  }
}
```

`axiom.plugin` is also accepted for compatibility. The module's default export
is called with an Express sub-app and a host context:

```js
export default function init(app, ctx) {
  app.get("/api/hello", (req, res) => res.json({ ok: true }));
  app.reg({ title: "My Skill", url: "/" }); // optional; default entry is added
  app.ws("/ws", (socket) => socket.send("hello"));
  ctx.ai.prompt("Summarize the current workspace");
}
```

If the app has both `index.html` and a JS module, `index.html` is served at
`/<name>/iframe/` and the module can add routes. Use `app.noUI()` for an
API-only skill that should not appear in the sidebar. Use
`app.reg({ url: "https://..." })` to point an entry at an external page.

Routes are namespaced:

- `/<name>` — host SPA address-bar route
- `/<name>/iframe/...` — skill UI and static assets
- `/<name>/api/...` — skill APIs
- `/<name>/ws` — skill WebSocket endpoint

### Workspace manifest

The host serves `GET /manifest.json` for the workspace it runs in:

```json
{ "title": "my-project · 46215f07", "orientation": "portrait" }
```

`title` defaults to the workspace directory name plus its short workdir hash:
the first 8 hex characters of the same hash used by
`abpilot://open/<endpoint>/<hash>/` (and by the desktop tray label). Two
worktrees with the same directory name therefore stay distinguishable. The CLI
UI shows that title in its sidebar and in `document.title`, so the browser tab
names the workspace it serves. Mobile clients use it to name the workspace and
skip services that do not publish the document, so this is the only place to
rename a workspace. `orientation` is `portrait` (the default) or
`landscape`: a mobile client locks the workspace screen to it, so only ask for
`landscape` when the UI works at that aspect ratio. Values are trimmed and
lower-cased; anything else falls back to `portrait`. A skill app can replace the
document, or single fields, through `app.manifest` (`ctx.manifest` is the same
object):

```js
export default function init(app, ctx) {
  app.manifest.replace({ title: "Roadmap", icon: "map", orientation: "landscape" });
  app.manifest.get(); // { title: "Roadmap", orientation: "landscape", icon: "map" }
  app.manifest.clear(); // back to the default label and portrait
}
```

Overrides merge in plugin order, so a later skill app wins for the fields it
sets. The endpoint is outside the skill namespace (`/<name>/manifest.json` is a
skill route); requests only get a metadata document, never UI access.

`GET`/`HEAD /manifest.json` is also exempt from the external-access guard: a
peer's mobile client needs the title and orientation before it can list and open
the workspace, even while the UI itself is not exposed. The document holds only
the workspace name and orientation (plus whatever fields a skill app adds), so it
leaks no UI, data, or routes. Every other path keeps the default-deny behaviour.

`ctx.ai` exposes:

```text
available, active, prompt, create, send, status, messages, forms,
replyForm, cancelForm, session, agents, models, switchAgent,
switchModel, interrupt, fork, focus
```

### Skill app login

Login is owned by the skill app: it keeps its own credentials, session cookies,
and login page. The host only mirrors the resulting account in the sidebar so
the user can see who is signed in and where to sign in.

Declare the entry in `package.json` so the sidebar can offer sign-in before any
skill code runs:

```json
{
  "abpilot": {
    "plugin": "index.js",
    "auth": {
      "login": "/login",   // page to open inside /<name>/iframe
      "logout": "/logout"  // optional page to open after signing out
    }
  }
}
```

`"auth": "/login"` is shorthand for `{ "login": "/login" }`. Both paths are
relative to the skill app, and an absolute URL opens in a new tab instead.

Report the account from the skill once its own login route has authenticated the
user:

```js
export default function init(app, ctx) {
  app.auth.require({ login: "/login" }); // for apps without a manifest block
  app.auth.onLogout(async () => {
    // clear the app's own session
  });

  app.post("/api/login", (req, res) => {
    const user = authenticate(req);
    app.auth.setUser({ id: user.id, name: user.name, avatar: user.avatar, email: user.email });
    res.json({ ok: true });
  });

  app.post("/api/logout", (req, res) => {
    app.auth.clear();
    res.json({ ok: true });
  });
}
```

`app.auth` also exposes `user()`, `status()`, `login(path)`, `logoutPath(path)`.
`ctx.auth` is the same object. The host mirror is in memory: after a restart the
app reports the user again on its next request. The app's own session can be
persisted in `ctx.store` (the shared local store); the host never stores skill
credentials itself.

The sidebar footer is hidden when no skill app declares a login. With a
declaration and no reported user it becomes a **Sign in to <app>** entry that
opens the declared login page in the content iframe; once a user is reported it
shows the avatar, name, and email with **Open <app>** and **Sign out** in a
menu. Accounts are local-only: external peers always get `{ apps: [] }`.

## Host APIs

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/health` | Version and health |
| GET | `/api/config` | Workspace, skills roots, gateway info |
| GET | `/api/plugins` | Skill app entries (`loading` while scanning) |
| GET | `/api/auth` | Login entries and the account each skill app reported (local only) |
| GET | `/api/auth/events` | SSE login-state changes (local only) |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | Sign out of one skill app by `name` (local UI only; requires JSON and `X-ABPilot-Client: cli-ui`) |
| GET | `/api/gateway` | Gateway/daemon/routes/services status |
| POST | `/api/gateway/refresh` | Re-read runtime and force status refresh |
| GET | `/api/gateway/routes` | Gateway workdir routes |
| GET | `/api/gateway/services` | Registered desktop services |
| GET | `/api/external` | Exposure status, endpoint, external URL, capabilities, and skill grants |
| POST | `/api/external` | Enable/disable external access or update policy (local UI only; requires JSON and `X-ABPilot-Client: cli-ui`) |
| GET | `/api/external/skills` | Skill app grants and current policy |
| PATCH | `/api/external/skills/<name>` | Enable/disable one skill app (local UI only; requires JSON and `X-ABPilot-Client: cli-ui`) |
| GET | `/api/opencode` | AI chat availability |
| GET/POST | `/api/opencode/active` | Current chat session |
| GET/POST | `/api/opencode/prefs` | Agent/model preferences |
| GET | `/api/opencode/models` | Trimmed, cached model/provider catalog |
| GET | `/api/opencode/agents` | Trimmed, cached agent list |
| GET | `/api/opencode/sessions` | Cursor-paginated session list projection |
| GET | `/api/opencode/transcript` | Cursor-paginated message projection (`sessionID`, `limit`, `cursor`, `order`) |
| GET | `/api/opencode/message` | One projected message (`sessionID`, `messageID`) |
| GET | `/api/opencode/attachment/<id>` | Inline image referenced by a projected message |
| GET | `/api/opencode/notify` | SSE focus/active/prefs events |
| WS | `/api/opencode/ws` | AI chat control channel |
| * | `/opencode/*` | OpenCode reverse proxy (Basic auth injected) |
| * | `/gateway/*` | Gateway reverse proxy |

## Security

- The UI has **no authentication**. It binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. Only use
  `--host 0.0.0.0` on a trusted machine/network.
- External access is **disabled by default**. Enabling it publishes the UI and
  the AI-chat/gateway surfaces; skill apps stay private until
  `capabilities.skills` is turned on. Enable it only for trusted peers, and
  narrow `ctx.external` policies for sensitive skill-app routes.
- Once enabled, external peers get only the UI, the AI-chat API, the gateway
  proxy, and the skill apps that are enabled. `capabilities.chat`,
  `capabilities.gateway`, and `capabilities.skills` gate whole surfaces;
  `skills.<name>.enabled` gates one app. Denied skill apps are also hidden
  from `/api/plugins`.
- Account skills (sign-in, endpoints, device management) treat every mutating
  route as host-only even for same-account peers: a remote caller cannot sign
  the host out, delete its endpoint, or trigger verification emails.
- The UI rejects non-loopback `Host` headers, so DNS rebinding cannot make a
  page same-origin with it. State-changing host APIs require JSON plus either
  the `X-ABPilot-Client: cli-ui` marker or a same-origin browser request, so a
  cross-site form or `no-cors` fetch cannot drive them.
- External requests are identified by daemon-injected
  `x-abpilot-endpoint-id`; they are rejected while external access is disabled
  unless a skill app's authorizer accepts that caller. The external policy API
  is local-only and external responses omit host paths, the state file, skill
  roots, and the full policy document.
- Skill app accounts are local-only as well: `/api/auth` returns `{ apps: [] }`
  to external peers, and `/api/auth/logout` requires the CLI UI client marker, so
  a skill app or remote page cannot sign the user out silently.
- `ctx.external.authorize` runs for requests the daemon already marked as
  external, including while the global toggle is off (it cannot turn the toggle
  on by itself), and fails closed on errors or timeouts. Local-only APIs
  (`/api/external`, `/api/auth/logout`, `/api/config`) still reject accepted
  callers.
- JS skill apps are imported into the host process and have full Node.js access.
  Only load skills from trusted directories. Static apps are served as files but
  still run in the browser with the page's origin.
- Every skill app, the UI, and the workspace share one
  `127.0.0.1:<port>` origin, so browser storage (localStorage, IndexedDB, cache)
  is shared between them. Treat skill apps and workspace pages as mutually
  trusting; the host does not isolate their storage. Credentials are never
  placed there (`ctx.store` lives server-side), and the daemon strips
  `Cookie`/`Authorization` on peer-bound traffic, but a malicious local page
  could still read another page's storage.
- The OpenCode password is generated per process and never sent to the browser;
  the browser only sees the local proxy.
- `/gateway/*` exposes whatever the loopback gateway exposes locally. It is not
  intended as a public ingress.
- `/built-in/**` is never mounted by this CLI.

## Environment variables

```text
ABPILOT_UI_PORT
ABPILOT_UI_HOST
ABPILOT_GATEWAY_URL
ABPILOT_RUNTIME_FILE
ABPILOT_DESKTOP_DIR
ABPILOT_CLI_STATE
ABPILOT_OPENCODE_BIN
```

## Layout

```text
cli/
  bin/abpilot.js          CLI entry
  lib/cli.js              argument parsing and commands
  lib/ui.js               HTTP/WS host, APIs, plugin mounting
  lib/external.js         desktop exposure registration and external policy
  lib/gateway.js          runtime discovery + gateway status/proxy helpers
  lib/opencode-server.js  private opencode child process
  lib/opencode-chat.js    chat bridge used by UI and skill apps
  lib/plugins.js          skill discovery / manifest parsing
  lib/store.js            JSON state store (shared with skill apps via ctx.store)
  ui/                     React/Vite UI (build to ui/dist)
  test/                   smoke tests
```
